exposure: Birth weight group (very low birth weight vs. preterm infants >1500g)
outcome: Gut microbiota composition (phyla and genera levels)
cohort: The study included 58 very low birth weight infants and 34 preterm infants with birth weights > 1500 g.
finding: Very low birth weight infants exhibit distinct gut microbiota characteristics during their first two months of life compared to preterm infants with birth weights > 1500 g, with factors like probiotic use, delivery mode, and premature rupture of membranes significantly influencing specific bacterial populations.
mod_finding: Delivery mode significantly influenced the relative abundances of Streptococcus, Clostridium_sensu_stricto_1, and Pseudomonas in very low birth weight infants.
